deals.description: Closed 2025-01-23. Dream Finders bought the majority of the homebuilding business of Georgia-based Liberty Communities, LLC (certain assets and assumed liabilities) for $112.7 million in cash; the former owner also received a redeemable noncontrolling interest in DFH Liberty, LLC valued at $8.1 million, with rights to a share of future earnings above a threshold. Trade press (The Real Deal, 2025-02-03) adds that the purchase included Liberty's offsite manufacturing and component import businesses.
deals.map_impact: No rank row merges (Liberty is not in the top 100). Dream Finders (#14) entered Atlanta and enlarged Greenville, South Carolina; Liberty's volume is inside the Dream Finders row.
deals.source_title: Dream Finders Homes 10-Q for Q2 2025, Business Acquisitions note

deals.description: Announced as completed on 2025-01-31: privately held Drees Homes bought San Antonio-based Monticello Homes, a roughly 30-year-old builder. Price and closings not disclosed in the source. Founder Wayne Moravits stays as a consultant for at least a year.
deals.map_impact: No rank row merges. Drees (#37) adds San Antonio and now builds in all four big Texas markets (Dallas-Fort Worth, Houston, Austin, San Antonio).
deals.source_title: HousingWire / The Builder's Daily: Drees Forays Into San Antonio With Monticello Homes Purchase (2025-01-31)

deals.description: Closed 2025-02-04 per Construction Briefing: Defy Investments, a newly formed investment company under Rival Holdings, bought Indianapolis builder Davis Homes. Price undisclosed. The buyer described a buy-and-hold approach and plans to test construction technology (HousingWire interview, 2025-02-06).
deals.map_impact: No change to the top-100 map: neither party is ranked. Example of a financial (non-builder) buyer taking a private regional builder.
deals.source_title: Construction Briefing: What's driving the consolidation of US homebuilders? (2025-05-13)

deals.description: Reported 2025-02-07 as acquired: Canada-based Empire Communities bought Charlotte, North Carolina builder SouthCraft Builders, an attainable-price builder that keeps its operations and leadership under Empire. Terms not disclosed. Builder Advisor Group advised SouthCraft. Follows Empire's 2024 purchase of Covington Homes in Colorado.
deals.map_impact: No rank row merges. Empire (#61, listed as Empire Homes) deepens Charlotte with a lower price point; SouthCraft's volume now counts inside Empire.
deals.source_title: HousingWire / The Builder's Daily: Empire Building: SouthCraft Expands U.S. Footprint, Scale (2025-02-07)

deals.description: Closed 2025-02-10 (previously announced). Lennar bought the homebuilding operations of Fayetteville, Arkansas-based Rausch Coleman, which delivered about 5,300 homes at an average price of about $230,000 in calendar 2024. Millrose Properties, just spun off from Lennar, bought Rausch Coleman's land and Lennar holds options on it. Lennar did not disclose a price; Construction Briefing (2025-05-13) cited a $900 million transaction value.
deals.map_impact: Rausch Coleman no longer exists as a separate ranked builder: its roughly 5,300 annual closings are inside Lennar (#2). Lennar gained new markets in Arkansas (including Bentonville/Fayetteville and Little Rock), Tulsa, Birmingham and Kansas City. First builder acquisition financed with Millrose land banking, the template later used for New Home Co / Landsea.
deals.source_title: Lennar press release: Lennar Completes Acquisition of Rausch Coleman Homes (2025-02-10)

deals.description: Reported on 2025-03-10 as set to close that night (a separate closing confirmation was not found). Davidson Homes bought Columbus, Georgia-based Evermore Homes (formerly American Southern Homes), a roll-up of Grayhawk Homes (Georgia), Stoneridge Homes (Alabama) and Dorn Homes (Arizona) that sold after running into capital constraints. Terms not disclosed.
deals.map_impact: No rank row merges. Davidson (#43) gets its first Arizona position plus more Southeast volume; Evermore's brands fold into Davidson.
deals.source_title: HousingWire / The Builder's Daily: Davidson Homes Seals Down Last Details To Acquire Evermore Homes (2025-03-10)

deals.description: Effective 2025-04-01 (announced 2025-03-28 by Sumitomo Forestry America): Dallas-based Brightland Homes was consolidated under Rockville, Maryland-based DRB Group. This is an internal combination of two Sumitomo Forestry builders, not a purchase from a third party. Per HousingWire (2025-04-16) the combined DRB spans 14 states and 19 divisions, expected about 9,000 closings in 2025, and is led by DRB chief executive Ronny Salameh.
deals.map_impact: Brightland Homes disappears as a separate ranked row; its volume is in DRB Group (#15, parent Sumitomo Forestry). DRB's leader stayed; Brightland's separate leadership did not continue at the top.
deals.source_title: Brightland Homes press page: Brightland Homes to Consolidate Under DRB Group (release dated 2025-03-28)

deals.acquirer: Iida Group Holdings (via Arnest One America)
deals.description: Announcement date (Iida's Tokyo filing is dated 2025-04-07; summarized 2025-04-14): Iida's subsidiary Arnest One set up Arnest One America to subscribe for new shares giving it 60% of PMCO Holdings, the parent of Atlanta-area builder Patrick Malloy Communities, for about $55.1 million, with closing expected in late April 2025. PMCO had 2024 sales of $117 million and operating profit of $18.8 million. HousingWire (2025-08-04) put the investment at about $52 million and the implied whole-company value just under $90 million, and treated the deal as newly public in late July 2025; a closing date was not confirmed.
deals.map_impact: No change to the top-100 map (target unranked). First US builder controlled by Iida Group, a new Japanese entrant alongside Sekisui House, Daiwa House and Sumitomo Forestry.
deals.source_title: FilingReader summary of Iida Group Holdings notice: subsidiary to acquire US housing firm (2025-04-14)

deals.description: Closed 2025-05-02. Dream Finders bought Atlanta homebuilder Green River Builders, Inc.; cash consideration was $32.8 million as first reported in the Q2 2025 10-Q (purchase accounting was preliminary). Reported in the Southeast segment.
deals.map_impact: No rank row merges. Second Atlanta acquisition in 2025 for Dream Finders (#14), after Liberty Communities.
deals.source_title: Dream Finders Homes 10-Q for Q2 2025, Business Acquisitions note

deals.description: Closed 2025-05-14: Scott Felder Homes, the Central Texas builder owned by Kansas City private equity firm Platform Ventures, bought Olivia Clarke Homes, a builder founded in 2020 with five Dallas-Fort Worth communities. Olivia Clarke keeps its name and founder Jennifer Johnson stays. Terms not disclosed; Builder Advisor Group was exclusive advisor.
deals.map_impact: No change to the top-100 map: neither party is ranked. Private-equity-backed platform adding Dallas-Fort Worth to Austin, San Antonio and Denver.
deals.source_title: HousingWire / The Builder's Daily: Platform's Scott Felder Buys Olivia Clarke In Strategic Stretch (2025-05-14)

deals.acquirer: The New Home Company (Apollo funds); now Risewell Homes
deals.description: Closed 2025-06-25 (announced 2025-05-12). Apollo-backed New Home Co, through Lido Holdco, completed a cash tender offer and merger for Nasdaq-listed Landsea Homes at $11.30 per share; about 83.3% of shares were tendered and Landsea was delisted. Trade press valued the deal at about $1.2 billion, with Apollo funds putting in $650 million of new equity and Millrose Properties providing land banking capital. New Home chief executive Matthew Zaist became president and CEO of the combined company; all of Landsea's executive officers left office and its board, including John Ho, resigned.
deals.map_impact: Landsea Homes disappears as a separate builder and the combined company is the #27 row, now named Risewell Homes (about 4,000 closings a year across roughly 10 markets per HousingWire). Leadership is New Home's; Landsea's leadership left. Millrose is the land banker of record on this deal.
deals.source_title: Landsea Homes Corp. 8-K filed 2025-06-25 (completion of merger with Lido Holdco / New Home Co)

deals.description: Closed 2025-09-25 US time (announced 2025-09-17). Stanley Martin bought the assets and operations of Greensboro, North Carolina builder Windsor Homes: land, homes and staff in the Triad (Greensboro, Winston-Salem, High Point) and Wilmington. Windsor delivered 334 homes in 2024 on about $124 million of revenue and had about 2,100 lots secured. Price not disclosed; Daiwa House said the effect on its results is not significant.
deals.map_impact: No rank row merges (Windsor unranked). Stanley Martin (#18) adds the North Carolina Triad and Wilmington and about 2,100 lots; first of three Stanley Martin acquisitions in under a year (United Homes Group and Holiday Builders followed in 2026).
deals.source_title: Daiwa House Industry press release: Stanley Martin Homes Has Acquired the Homebuilding Business of Windsor Homes (2025-09-26)

deals.description: Closed in October 2025 (exact day not disclosed; trade press reported it as done on 2025-10-10). D.R. Horton bought the homebuilding operations of Greenville, South Carolina-based SK Builders for about $80 million in cash: about 160 homes in inventory, 260 lots and a backlog of 110 sold homes, plus control of about 1,320 more lots through purchase contracts. The sellers kept their land development business (HousingWire).
deals.map_impact: No rank row merges (SK Builders is not in the top 100). D.R. Horton (#1) deepens Greenville/Spartanburg; the sellers continue as a land developer.
deals.source_title: D.R. Horton 10-Q for the quarter ended 2025-12-31 (SK Builders acquisition)

deals.acquirer: None (company-run review of strategic alternatives, including a sale or merger)
deals.description: Review ended without a deal, disclosed 2025-10-19/20. On 2025-05-19 United Homes Group's board formed a special committee of independent directors to review strategic alternatives. In October 2025 the committee concluded the company should stay independent given market conditions; four independent directors then said they would resign after controlling stockholder and executive chairman Michael Nieri declined to step down from that role, and two other directors also resigned.
deals.map_impact: No map change at the time: United Homes Group (#56) stayed independent. It set up the February 2026 agreement to sell to Stanley Martin at $1.18 per share.
deals.source_title: United Homes Group 8-K filed 2025-10-20 (conclusion of strategic review; director resignations)

deals.description: Closed 2026-01-14 (announced 2026-01-16). Single-family rental owner Invitation Homes bought Atlanta-based ResiBuilt, a fee builder of build-to-rent communities, for $89 million plus up to $7.5 million of incentive payments. It came with 23 active building contracts and an option on about 1,500 lots; no land transferred. ResiBuilt has built more than 4,200 homes since 2018 in Georgia, Florida and the Carolinas. Former parent Resicap stays independent.
deals.map_impact: No change to the top-100 map (neither party is a ranked for-sale builder). A rental landlord bringing a homebuilder in-house; relevant to build-to-rent lot demand in the Southeast.
deals.source_title: The Real Deal: Invitation Homes Buys ResiBuilt for $89M (2026-01-19)

deals.description: Announced 2026-03-10: Tokyo-based Hajime Construction, an Iida Group company, took a 51% stake and management control of Utah builder Wright Homes (founded 1994, Wasatch Front). Founder Derek Wright and his team stay as operators and minority owners and the brand continues. Price not stated in the source; a closing date was not confirmed.
deals.map_impact: No change to the top-100 map (target unranked). Second US builder stake for Iida Group after Patrick Malloy Communities; one of four Japanese-buyer deals that opened 2026.
deals.source_title: HousingWire: Hajime Construction Buys 51% of Utah Builder Wright Homes (2026-03-12)

deals.description: Agreement signed and business transfer executed 2026-03-19 US time (2026-03-20 Japan time). Trumark bought the single-family homebuilding business of Sumner, Washington-based JK Monarch: land, homes and staff in the Seattle metro area. JK Monarch delivered 59 homes in 2024 on about $53 million of revenue and had about 600 lots secured at the end of February 2026. Price not disclosed; Daiwa House said the effect on its results is minimal.
deals.map_impact: No rank row merges (JK Monarch unranked). Trumark (#66) adds a Washington division, its first market outside California and Colorado; Daiwa House's three US builders (Stanley Martin, CastleRock, Trumark) now reach the Pacific Northwest.
deals.source_title: Daiwa House Industry press release: Trumark Companies to Acquire the Single-Family Housing Business of Monarch (2026-03-23)

deals.description: Announced 2026-04-21: definitive agreement to buy substantially all assets of Fayetteville, Arkansas luxury builder Buffington Homes (founded 2010; nine active or coming-soon communities; owns or controls over 1,500 lots; prices from the $400,000s to over $1 million). Terms not disclosed; closing was expected in Toll's fiscal third quarter (May-July 2026); no separate closing release was found. Toll's 16th builder acquisition since 1995. Builder Advisor Group advised the seller.
deals.map_impact: No rank row merges (Buffington unranked). Toll Brothers (#9) enters Fayetteville/Bentonville in northwest Arkansas with 1,500+ lots; Buffington staff join Toll, partners Clay Carlton and Mike Lamberth focus on land, co-owner Mike Buffington exits.
deals.source_title: Toll Brothers press release: Toll Brothers to Acquire Private Home Builder in Northwest Arkansas (2026-04-21)

deals.description: Closed 2026-05-04 (announced 2026-02-23; merger agreement dated 2026-02-22). Stanley Martin acquired Nasdaq-listed United Homes Group by merger for $1.18 per share in cash, an enterprise value of about $221 million; the stock and warrants were delisted. The executive officers listed in the closing 8-K, including chief executive Jack Micenko and executive chairman Michael Nieri, ceased to be officers at closing.
deals.map_impact: United Homes Group (#56, 1,192 closings in the ranking) is now a wholly owned subsidiary of Stanley Martin (#18): the two rows share one owner, Daiwa House. United Homes' top leadership left at closing. Adds Greenville, Spartanburg, Clemson, Columbia and Myrtle Beach, South Carolina and Augusta, Georgia to Stanley Martin (per HousingWire).
deals.source_title: United Homes Group 8-K filed 2026-05-04 (completion of merger with Stanley Martin Homes)

deals.description: Unsolicited proposals, rejected. Dream Finders privately proposed to buy Beazer for $28.50 per share in February 2026 and $29.00 in March 2026; after being turned down it went public on 2026-05-11 with a $25.75 per share all-cash offer (about $704 million of equity value), which Beazer's board rejected the same day as undervaluing the company (book value $41.83 per share). Date shown is the public disclosure. Later 2026 coverage reports the two signed a definitive agreement in August 2026; that deal belongs to the May-2026-onward list.
deals.map_impact: No map change from these proposals themselves. They put Beazer (#21) in play; if the later August 2026 agreement closes, the Beazer row would sit under Dream Finders (#14).
deals.source_title: Jacksonville Daily Record: Beazer Homes rejects Dream Finders offer (2026-05-11)

deals.description: Closed 2026-05-14 (announced 2026-02-13). Sumitomo Forestry bought NYSE-listed Tri Pointe Homes for $47.00 per share in cash, about $4.5 billion in total (about $4.1 billion of equity). Tri Pointe was delisted and is a wholly owned subsidiary of Sumitomo Forestry America, keeping its brand, Irvine home office and divisions. Chief executive Doug Bauer and president Tom Mitchell are expected to stay. Sumitomo says the enlarged group delivers about 15,000 homes a year in 18 states and targets 23,000 a year by 2030.
deals.map_impact: Tri Pointe (#19) is now owned by Sumitomo Forestry, the same parent as DRB Group (#15); added together the Sumitomo builders are roughly a top-five US builder by closings. Tri Pointe's rank row and leadership stay; it adds more than 160 communities in 13 states, mainly the West and coasts, to the Sumitomo group.
deals.source_title: Tri Pointe Homes 8-K exhibit 99.1: Sumitomo Forestry completes acquisition of Tri Pointe Homes (2026-05-14)

gaps: Web search budget for the session ran out part-way through, so builder-by-builder sweeps for 2025 to April 2026 deals by PulteGroup, Meritage, Taylor Morrison, Century Communities, LGI, M/I, Smith Douglas, Hovnanian, Green Brick, Clayton Properties Group, Ashton Woods / Starlight, David Weekley, Perry Homes, Mattamy, Brookfield Residential, Forestar and KB Home were only partly done. The searches that did run found no acquisition by those companies inside the window; this is 'not found', not 'confirmed none'.

JTW Advisors counts 18 US homebuilder deals in 2025 (cited by HousingWire); this file has 13 rows dated 2025 (11 purchases, one internal consolidation, one ended sale review). The remaining small private deals were not identified.

McGuinn Homes (#65) buying Columbia, South Carolina communities from Hurricane Builders (about 2025; Whelan Advisory / JTW involvement indicated in search results): the only source found is a Builder magazine article that could not be opened (site blocks automated access), so no row was written.

Sekisui House / M.D.C. integration (folding Woodside, Holt, Chesmar and M.D.C. into one Sekisui House U.S. organization, 2025-2026): seen only in search results pointing to Builder magazine, which could not be opened; no row written. The original M.D.C. purchase closed in April 2024, before this window.

Builder magazine (builderonline.com) M&A roundups could not be opened at all (403 to both fetch methods); BusinessWire, risewellhomes.com and Beazer's investor site also refused automated access. Facts were taken from SEC filings, company sites that loaded, HousingWire and other trade press instead.
Toll Brothers / Buffington Homes: no closing announcement found; Toll's Q3 FY2026 earnings release did not mention Buffington in the text retrieved. Status left as Announced.

Davidson Homes / Evermore Homes and both Iida Group stakes (Patrick Malloy Communities, Wright Homes): closing dates not confirmed from a source opened in this run. Purchase prices for Drees/Monticello, Empire/SouthCraft, Davidson/Evermore, Defy/Davis, Scott Felder/Olivia Clarke, Stanley Martin/Windsor, Trumark/JK Monarch and Toll/Buffington are not publicly disclosed.
Lennar / Rausch Coleman price: not disclosed by Lennar; the $900 million figure is from one trade article only.

Brookfield Residential and Kolter: a November 2026 HousingWire piece refers to Brookfield 'Kolter transactions' (investing in an operator before buying it); no detail or date could be confirmed, and it may fall after April 2026.
Perry Homes / MasterCraft Builder Group (announced 2024-12-03) and Lennar / WCH Homes (August 2024) were checked and fall before the window, so they are excluded.

Deals after 2026-04-30 seen in passing and left to the May-onward agent: Berkshire Hathaway / Taylor Morrison, Eastwood Homes / Peachtree Building Group (May 2026), Mungo Homes (Clayton) / McGuinn Homes (July 2026), Stanley Martin / Holiday Builders (announced 2026-07-16), Dream Finders / Beazer definitive agreement (August 2026), Century Communities / HistoryMaker Homes (announced 2026-10-08).
